limits_note: The free column's 'max upload file size 0.00001 Mb' is the vendor's own placeholder and should be read as 'no free upload', not as a number.
binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the 60 GB/day premium allowance is fine; what fails first is the one-day free retention, which makes the free tier unusable for a multi-part archive even before speed.

identity_cost.detail: E-mail signup; card and crypto through the host checkout.

reliability_note: Sharing a premium account blocks access immediately, per the payment page warning.
confidence_note: The vendor's payment page is client-rendered and returned no text to the reader; the comparison table and plan prices are the search index's render of that page. A direct read would raise this to documented.

price_per_tb_month: USD 30.54 per TiB-month (USD 50 for a 1.64 TiB allowance); USD 20.6 per TiB-month at 365 days
notes: Two vendor surfaces disagree on the free numbers by a factor of four, which is why the verdict does not rest on them: the premium price per TiB is USD 30, five times the best host compared. At 365 days, the vendor's own 60 GB/day is 21,900 GB = 19.92 TiB, so the annual plan costs USD 15.06 per TiB-month; a figure of USD 20.6 per TiB-month implies 300 / 20.6 = 14.6 TiB. The difference is 27%, and it moves DropGalaxy from worst-in-class on the annual plan to mid-table.
